# Kwasi Wiredu quote sources

9 passages attributed to Kwasi Wiredu in this archive, each with the locator that lets you find it in the work itself — and the one thing that most often goes wrong when people quote Wiredu.

[Quote source](https://www.philosophydef.com/quote-source) / Kwasi Wiredu

How to cite this author, and what circulates under the name that is not theirs to give.

## Sourcing profile

Language of the works

English

Cited here from

Articles including “The Concept of Truth in the Akan Language,” “The Need for Conceptual Decolonization in African Philosophy,” and “Democracy and Consensus in African Traditional Politics,” several of them collected in Cultural Universals and Particulars (1996).

How to cite it

Journal title, volume, and year for the article as first published, or the chapter in Cultural Universals and Particulars — and say which, because the reprint and the original have different locators.

Where quotations of this author go wrong

Wiredu writes in English about concepts carried in Akan, and his method — conceptual decolonization — turns on the fact that a word like “truth” does not map cleanly onto the Akan term he is discussing. Quoting him in English to make a claim about Akan thought, without the term he was working with, produces a sentence he would not accept.

## Frequently asked questions

### Where can I check quotations attributed to Kwasi Wiredu?

Journal title, volume, and year for the article as first published, or the chapter in Cultural Universals and Particulars — and say which, because the reprint and the original have different locators. This archive cites Kwasi Wiredu from Articles including “The Concept of Truth in the Akan Language,” “The Need for Conceptual Decolonization in African Philosophy,” and “Democracy and Consensus in African Traditional Politics,” several of them collected in Cultural Universals and Particulars (1996). Every passage listed on this page carries that locator, so it can be found in any edition of the work.

### What is the most common mistake when quoting Kwasi Wiredu?

Wiredu writes in English about concepts carried in Akan, and his method — conceptual decolonization — turns on the fact that a word like “truth” does not map cleanly onto the Akan term he is discussing. Quoting him in English to make a claim about Akan thought, without the term he was working with, produces a sentence he would not accept.

### What language did Kwasi Wiredu write in?

English. For an author writing in English the wording is settled at source, but editions and titles are not — see the citation note above.
